turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on comparatives (-er, more ... than)?
turns.tutor:
Rule: short words add -er (easy - easier); long words use more; then add than.
Right: "A horse is heavier than a dog." Wrong: "A horse is heavyer than a dog." Heavy ends in y, so the y changes to i before -er.
My example: "A tiger is more dangerous than a cat." I think: dangerous is a long word, so no -er. I use more, then than.
Now you try. Complete:
"Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
